html:
The Battle of Karnal was fought on 24 February 1739 at Karnal, north of Delhi, between the Persian army of Nader Shah and the army of the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah.

The Mughal army was far larger, but poorly led and divided. Nader's disciplined troops with muskets and mobile artillery broke it in a few hours. The Mughal emperor was taken, and Nader marched into Delhi with him. The victory opened the road for the sack of the capital and the seizure of the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor. It also revealed how weak the Mughal state had become. See Nader Shah's invasion of India.
